- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 10–30% for near-term (1–7d) horizon.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.33) or volatile, model often underestimates or spikes too early; increase forecast for 1–7d horizon to align with sentiment reversal.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > 2x recent mean), model frequently overcorrects downward; apply a “lag correction” — reduce forecast by 20–40% for 1–3d horizon.
- For 14–30d horizon, model often fails to capture mean reversion; if sentiment is neutral or slightly positive, apply a “mean reversion bias” — forecast should be closer to 30d moving average of history.
- If sentiment history shows strong upward momentum (e.g., 3+ consecutive +0.67), model tends to overreact; cap forecast at 1.5x recent 7d high for 1–7d horizon.
- If sentiment is flat or negative for 3+ days, model often underestimates true drop; add 5–15% buffer to forecast for 1–7d horizon to account for sentiment lag.
